label: live
test: step corrections survive reload and undo launches the requested redo with visible history
expected: the Jevellan web app "undo" screen, one step of the check "step corrections survive reload and undo launches the requested redo with visible history", at desktop-light, rendered completely and legibly

cosmetic: Two identical red error banners read 'No model can run this step right now: disabled, disabled, …' (eight times each). They add no useful detail and look like a duplicated or leftover state between the undone step and the redo.
The undone Step 1 card uses faint grey struck-through text, including the 'STEP 1 · IMPLEMENT' header and the HANDOFF/DONE labels. It is still readable but has low contrast.

Sidebar conversation titles and meta lines are cut off with ellipses (e.g. 'Change the value to three, the…', 'Waiting for you · Browser fixture · d…'). This is expected truncation, and the full title is shown in the main pane.
The dashed 'corrected:' chips wrap onto a second line inside the Step 1 header row, so the header looks slightly uneven.
